answer: Interleaved arrival clock.** Each identity must keep its request arrivals spread across time: a controller checks that no more than k actions land in any short window, and that gaps between actions follow a minimum spacing. A vine of correlated bursts fails this shape check even when each burst looks valid alone. The bridge rule is that an identity's first actions must be spaced wider than its later ones, so instant mass registration is impossible. A lantern signal — a short probe sent at random — confirms liveness across the spacing.
